reranked_evidence.title: South India leads India's nursing workforce as national ratio remains below WHO benchmark - The South First
reranked_evidence.snippet: # South India leads India’s nursing workforce as national ratio remains below WHO benchmark. > ***Synopsis:** Parliamentary data reveal a stark regional divide in India’s nursing workforce, with Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu accounting for nearly half of the country’s registered hospital nurses. South India has emerged as the country’s nursing powerhouse, with Kerala, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu accounting for nearly half of India’s registered hospital nursing workforce and recording some of the country’s highest nurse-population ratios, according to data tabled in Parliament. A written reply by Union Health Minister JP Nadda in the Rajya Sabha on 21 July states that India had 46.02 lakh registered nursing personnel as of 31 December 2025, translating to a nurse-population ratio of 2.60 per 1,000 people. “As per the Indian Nursing Council (INC) records, there are 46.02 lakh nursing personnel registered in the country as on 31st December, 2025, giving a nurse to population ratio of 2.60 nurses per 1000 population,” Nadda said in response to a starred question.

Cipla Q1 net profit tumbles 39% to ₹789 crore; stock falls - ET Manufacturing
reranked_evidence.snippet: The company’s consolidated revenue from operations inched up 2.33 per cent to ₹7,119.28 crore during the first quarter, compared to ₹6,957.47 crore in the corresponding period of the previous fiscal. Cipla on Thursday reported a 39.19 per cent year-on-year drop in its consolidated net profit for the quarter ended June 30, 2022, bringing it down to ₹789.05 crore. The company had clocked a net profit of ₹1,297.62 crore in the same quarter last year. Total income for the quarter also moved up slightly to ₹7,330.18 crore, up from ₹7,216.03 crore last year. Adding to the margin pressure, total expenses stood at ₹6,248.25 crore, a jump from the ₹5,446.10 crore it spent during the same quarter last year. The company is currently contesting demand notices from the National Pharmaceutical Pricing Authority (NPPA) aggregating to a massive ₹2,011 crore (comprising a principal of ₹863 crore and an interest of ₹1,148 crore) for alleged overcharging on scheduled drugs. ## All about ETManufacturing industry right on your smartphone!
